messages.subject: fixed error in check_ML_vs_BSM()
messages.subject_clean: fixed error in check_ML_vs_BSM()
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

A correspondent noted an error in non-stratified Biogeographical Stochastic Mapping (BSM), in the check function check_ML_vs_BSM() at the end of the script:

> Calculating BSM means for node #:139 Error in if (stratified == TRUE) { : argument is of length zero

She handily sent the files -- it turned out to be a simple problem with an error check that I introduced to fill in the "stratified" variable, except it didn't fill it in all cases.

If you re-install BioGeoBEARS from GitHub, check_ML_vs_BSM() should work now.

Cheers!
Nick

Hi Nick, how are you?

Man, I am getting this error when I try to "shortcut" the run to the parameters that converged.

It worked well for a DEC model, but when I try with a DEC+J i get the following error message:

check_BioGeoBEARS_run() says: STOP ERROR: 1 row(s) of the BioGeoBEARS_run_object$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table are set to be 'free', but they have starting values ('init') outside of the specified min/max.

Fix manually, or run fix_BioGeoBEARS_params_minmax(). Printing these rows to screen....

type init min max est note
d free 0 1e-12 5 0 works
desc
d anagenesis: rate of 'dispersal' (range expansion)
Error in check_BioGeoBEARS_run(decj.potamo) :
check_BioGeoBEARS_run() says: STOP ERROR: 1 row(s) of the BioGeoBEARS_run_object$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table are set to be 'free', but they have starting values ('init') outside of the specified min/max.

Fix manually, or run fix_BioGeoBEARS_params_minmax(). Printing these rows to screen....

I tried to play around with min values to 0, but still getting the error. Should I change the init value to 0.00001, for example?

Cheers

JP

messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] PDF printing fails
messages.subject_clean: [BioGeoBEARS] PDF printing fails
messages.body_plain:
Hi -- this error happened awhile back (6 months + I think) because of a change in how the APE package plots trees.  The BioGeoBEARS code uses some of this internal APE code.  What *should* happen is that BioGeoBEARS checks your version of APE, and uses the appropriate code from before or after the APE switch.

The most obvious way this check wouldn't happen would be if you actually have not got BioGeoBEARS updated to the GitHub version 1.1, or if you have the GitHub version but also have the old CRAN version (0.21) installed in a different "lib" directory.  Sometimes it seems that you can have the new version installed, but the functions of the old version of the code.

See these tools to try and root out old versions:

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/biogeobears/packageVersion%7Csort:date/biogeobears/2f9etrphhmg/0Jg1YIoOBwAJ

(conceivably, they might have changed APE back to the old plotting method, which worked better IMHO, but it doesn't look like APE has been updated in the last few days on CRAN; I can't speak to a GitHub version of APE)

Cheers!
Nick

messages.body_plain:
Hi -- the firewall issue shouldn't matter all all now that the script uses the GitHub install instead of source() on online files -- assuming you actually successfully installed the updated version from GitHub, *and* removed any old versions installed in R, see hints on doing this: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/biogeobears/detach%7Csort:date/biogeobears/2f9etrphhmg/0Jg1YIoOBwAJ

But, if you want to download all the updated BioGeoBEARS R files that you used to use source() opn, all you have to do is:

1. https://github.com/nmatzke/BioGeoBEARS
2. Go to the green Clone or download button
3. Click Download Zip
4. Unzip somewhere. The R source files are in the "R" subdirectory
5a. write out a bunch of source() commands to source the exact location on your hard drive for each file, or (easier)
5b. use the BioGeoBEARS sourceall() command to source everything in that R directory

All that said, it would be easier to just make sure the old installs are gone (just keep repeating library(BioGeoBEARS) and the various detach / remove.packages commands at

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/biogeobears/detach%7Csort:date/biogeobears/2f9etrphhmg/0Jg1YIoOBwAJ

...until library(BioGeoBEARS) no longer works, then and then just install the new GitHub version, assuming your firewall lets you install anything from GitHub.

Cheers,
Nick

OK, try it now. Cheers!
Nick

(PS: background:
rexpokit -- the updated version is at both CRAN and GitHub, but the CRAN version is much easier to install as it contains FORTRAN
cladoRcpp -- the updated version is at both CRAN and GitHub, but the CRAN version is much easier to install as it contains C++
BioGeoBEARS -- the updated version is only at GitHub, but is "pure R" so is (should be) easy to install from GitHub
)

It looks like there may be a non-ASCII character in the DESCRIPTION file which weirds out your system for some reason.  This surprises me as I typically use a plain-text editor, but I can see. I am traveling but I can attempt to fix this in a day or two.

Nick

messages.body_plain:
Hi Nick,

Happy Holidays! I have a question about processing BSM output that I am struggling to figure out:

For my study I am following the approach of Xing and Ree 2017 (https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1616063114) who used LAGRANGE to calculate a rolling speciation rate for each region for 1 myr time bins along their tree(s). The per-capita speciation rate for a focal region for each 1 myr time bin was calculated as the number of in-situ speciation events occuring in that time bin divided by the number of lineages occuring in the region in the previous 1 myr time bin.

I have the numerator figured out using BioGeoBEARS and BSM. That wasn't hard because I could get the states reconstructed at each node (I used ML_marginal_prob_each_state_at_branch_top_AT_node in the results object for each map individually) and I know the age of each node so I could assign to a time bin.

The denominator is giving me trouble. The "number of lineages in a region" implies the number of branches reconstructed within the focal region at the cut-off of the previous bin. So for example, if I draw a line through my tree at 5 mya I would want to count all the branches currently in region A at that moment, so I can use that number to calculate the speciation rate in region A for the following time bin at 4 myr. The fact that we're dealing with branches and not nodes gives me trouble. For example, if there was an extirpation event where A was lost along a branch, I don't want to count that branch in the total number of lineages for A for the relevant time bin; however, it matters exactly where along that branch the extirpation event occurred if the branch is longer than the length of each time bin.

Do you have a recommendation for how I may do this using BSM output? Specifically, I want to count the number of branches currently in a given region at any given time point in the tree.

Thank you for your help as always,
Best,
Liz

Hi!  I think someone, or several people, have done this -- Julia Dupin
maybe?
(Or, maybe I did it and forgot!)

Basically you have to iterate through the BSM tables, and for each time
point, count the total number of branches, and then for each branch
existing at that time point, figure out what its range is, then tabulate.

If you don't find something obvious already published on this, we can
discuss further, it shouldn't be too hard.

Cheers!
Nick

Hi, 2 thoughts:

1. Make sure all these work (and install.packages them if they don't)

library(minqa)
library(optimx)
library(GenSA)

2. See also this thread, especially ways to make sure you don't have an old install of BioGeoBEARS hiding out causing problems:

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/biogeobears/%22Error$20in$20BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table$24est%5Bfree_params_TF%5D%22%7Csort:date/biogeobears/2f9etrphhmg/9E4x-ZQHAwAJ

...everyone has always eventually gotten it working after trying these things I think...

Cheers!
Nick

messages.subject_clean: Model testing!?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Nick and everyone

Is there a way to run a quick model test on our data to see with of the models fit better our data or the only way I can do that is to run all the models and once they are finished compare the lnls and aics?

Cheers

JP

messages.subject_clean: [BioGeoBEARS] Model testing!?
messages.body_plain:
Hi -- yeah, you have to have the maximized log likelihoods under each model, and then calculate AIC or AICc, before you can statistically compare them.

Cheers,
Nick
